questions.q: Identify the conjunction relationship: “Walk carefully, lest you should fall.”
questions.why: 'Lest … should' expresses a negative purpose (so that … not). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “She ____ her mother in looks and manner.”
questions.why: 'Take after' means to resemble a parent or relative. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the figure of speech: “The child is the father of the man.”
questions.why: An apparently absurd statement that holds a truth (GPSC 2026). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the error: “I am knowing the new doctor since last year.”
questions.why: 'Know' is a stative verb, and 'since' needs the present perfect: 'I have known'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to bury the hatchet”:
questions.why: Bury the hatchet = end a quarrel. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Spot the error: “She is senior than me by two years.”
questions.why: 'Senior', 'junior', 'superior', 'inferior' take 'to': 'senior to me'. GPSC-style practice item.

opts: He is more taller than I.
He is taller than me am.
questions.why: After 'than', 'I' (as in 'than I am') is the formal correct form; GPSC keys follow this. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “diligent”:
questions.why: 'Diligent' means hardworking; 'indolent' means lazy. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: “____ more you practise, ____ better you become.”
questions.why: 'The ... the' with comparatives shows proportion. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “The train reaches Mumbai ____ the morning.”
questions.why: 'In' is used with parts of the day (morning, afternoon, evening). GPSC-style practice item.
